red.focus: Distinguish relevant evidence from convincing evidence.
red.summary: Evidence can concern the issue without proving it. Learn how source reliability, context, and competing explanations influence a factfinder's assessment.
checklist: I can recognize relevant but weak evidence
I can explain why source reliability matters
I can compare evidence supporting opposing accounts

sections.title: Relevance only opens the door
sections.body_md: A witness says a driver was near the scene of a collision. That fact may be relevant, but it does not prove who drove the vehicle or caused the harm. Evidentiary weight concerns how strongly admitted information supports a disputed proposition. A court should not confuse the right to consider an item with a duty to believe it. Ask what the evidence shows, what it leaves unknown, and whether the legal issue requires a stronger connection.

Ask what the evidence shows, what it leaves unknown, and whether the legal issue requires a stronger connection.

sections.title: The source changes the weight
sections.body_md: A signed contemporaneous receipt may provide stronger evidence of payment than a person's distant memory, but even a document may contain errors or be forged. Assess origin, time, firsthand knowledge, consistency, and whether the item has been authenticated where required. A confident witness can be mistaken; an official record can be incomplete. The weight of evidence depends on the specific proposition and context, not merely whether the source looks formal or impressive.

sections.title: Compare competing accounts fairly
sections.body_md: Two witnesses remember different times. Rather than choosing the person with the most persuasive manner, examine opportunities to observe, documentary records, possible inconsistencies, and what each account actually establishes. The factfinder should explain how the evidence supports a reasoned conclusion under the applicable standard of proof. Legal fairness requires care because an unexamined assumption about credibility can change someone's liberty, livelihood, or reputation.

yellow.summary: A competent factfinder distinguishes eyewitness memory, documentary integrity, expert method, and independent support. Learn why admissibility and weight remain different inquiries.
checklist: I can identify factors affecting witness credibility
I can explain authentication and corroboration
I can distinguish admissibility from the weight of admitted material

sections.title: Memory is not a recording
sections.body_md: A witness may sincerely recall an event inaccurately. Stress, exposure time, suggestive questioning, and passage of time can influence memory. Credibility analysis asks what the person could observe, whether their account changed, and how independent evidence relates. It should not treat confidence as a scientific guarantee of accuracy or assume that visible nervousness proves dishonesty. The court must apply its jurisdiction's evidence rules while reasoning carefully from what the testimony can actually support.

The court must apply its jurisdiction's evidence rules while reasoning carefully from what the testimony can actually support.

sections.title: Documents need an origin
sections.body_md: A screenshot of a message may appear decisive but omit context or fail to establish who wrote it. Authentication is the process of showing an item is what its proponent claims, under applicable evidentiary law. Metadata, other records, or testimony may support it. Even an authenticated record may be incomplete or ambiguous. Do not equate successful authentication with proof that every statement inside the record is true. Each inference requires a separate explanation.

sections.title: Independent support adds value
sections.body_md: Two witnesses who independently observed an event may corroborate one another. Ten people repeating one rumor do not provide ten independent sources. A lawyer should track how information traveled and distinguish original observations from repeated narratives. Corroboration can strengthen an account, but contradictions also need to be assessed for significance rather than used to dismiss an entire witness automatically. Weight reflects the relation between each piece of evidence and the particular fact to be proved.

orange.focus: Assess expert and statistical evidence without overclaiming.
orange.summary: Technical evidence can aid legal reasoning but can also conceal unreliable assumptions. Examine method, base rates, causal inference, and the difference between group findings and a specific legal claim.
checklist: I can identify reliability questions for expert methods
I can distinguish statistical association from causal proof
I can explain why strong evidence must match the legal proposition

sections.title: Ask how the result was produced
sections.body_md: A forensic expert reports a laboratory match. The court needs to know which method was used, its error rates, whether procedures were followed, and what the result actually signifies. Qualifications alone do not make every conclusion reliable. Evidence rules vary on how experts are admitted and challenged; a lawyer should name the governing test. The factfinder must separate the expert's measured observation from the inference that a particular person committed a legal wrong.

sections.title: Group risk is not always individual cause
sections.body_md: A study may show higher disease rates among people exposed to a substance. That can support a population-level association but may not determine which source caused one person's illness. Confounding variables, selection effects, and incomplete records matter. A legal system may provide specific causal or evidentiary rules, which must be applied explicitly. An advanced argument distinguishes what the data estimate from what a liability conclusion additionally requires. Avoid treating scientific uncertainty as either automatic liability or proof that no harm occurred.

sections.title: Evidence must answer the real question
sections.body_md: A company may produce thousands of emails establishing that its staff worked hard, while the legal issue is whether a particular required notice was sent. The evidentiary weight of material depends on the proposition it supports, not its volume or prestige. Organize competing explanations by fact, source, and inference. State where the record remains inconclusive. Accurate limitation of a claim can be more persuasive than a sweeping assertion that available evidence does not justify.

black.focus: Critique the epistemic justice of evidence evaluation.
black.summary: Rules of evidence can promote accuracy while excluding people who lack access to recognized forms of proof. Design assessment practices that are reliable, transparent, and alert to unequal power.
checklist: I can evaluate credibility practices for structural bias
I can compare formal admissibility and actual truthfinding
I can propose accountable evaluation of algorithmic evidence

sections.title: An evidentiary rule can silence experience
sections.body_md: A person subjected to discrimination may lack documents because the institution committing the wrong controls the records. Conversely, untested testimony may wrongly accuse another person. Evidence doctrines manage risks in both directions. A doctoral account should examine whose accounts the institution systematically distrusts, which methods receive unwarranted prestige, and which safeguards could improve reliable participation. Treating every story as true or every official record as objective would be equally careless.

sections.title: Algorithms can amplify error
sections.body_md: A predictive model used in a legal proceeding may embed training bias, measurement errors, or opaque assumptions. A numerical score is not self-authenticating and does not replace the governing legal standard. The court should know what the model predicts, whether it generalizes to the relevant population, and what opportunities exist to challenge its use. An expert's technical vocabulary cannot substitute for public reasons when state power affects liberty or livelihood.

sections.title: Design evidence evaluation with humility
sections.body_md: Propose documented provenance, transparent expert methods, adversarial testing where appropriate, and reasons explaining how conflicting proof was assessed. Provide mechanisms to correct serious mistakes and assess the effect on marginalized groups. Do not claim that method eliminates human judgment. Instead, make the judgment reviewable and anchored in reliable facts. A legitimate legal order should give every person a meaningful chance to be believed when their evidence warrants it, and protection from unsupported accusations when it does not.
